On a reference sheet, a formula sheet or a summary,
state each formula in its general form.
Do not state it only for a specific example.
A reader looks a formula up to apply it to a new case,
and an example shows only one case.

::: {#exm-general-form-formula}

## Stating the chain rule

> ❌ $\frac{d(u^2)}{dw} = 2u \frac{du}{dw}$
>
> ✅ $\frac{d f(u)}{dw} = f'(u) \frac{du}{dw}$

The ❌ line is the chain rule for squaring only.
The ✅ line holds for every differentiable $f$,
and the squaring case follows by taking $f(u) = u^2$.

:::

Put a specific case on the sheet only as a labeled example next to the general formula.
